transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we're here to discuss the proposed $6,000,000 commitment to Northbridge Private Credit Fund IV. Before I make any decision on whether and on what conditions we sign the commitment agreement, I'd like to hear from compliance and fund operations. Please report any issues you've identified and any execution requirements or pre-signing actions we need to be aware of. The fund accepts commitments until the end of the month, so we have some time, but I want to make sure we've done our full pre-signing review before I decide.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compliance issue. This morning's compliance circular included a policy amendment that has not yet been circulated to the investment committee. The amendment caps our commitment to this fund strategy at exactly $5,000,000, requires qualified-purchaser certification before signing, and requires quarterly look-through reporting. This directly impacts the proposed $6,000,000 commitment — we would exceed the new cap by $1,000,000. Additionally, we cannot sign until qualified-purchaser certification is completed, and we would need to commit to quarterly look-through reporting as an ongoing obligation.

transcript.text: I have an important execution requirement to flag. I received the fund administrator's confirmation today that the first capital call will be exactly $1,200,000 within 5 business days after signing, and treasury can ring-fence that amount in cash. Critically, the confirmation states a fixed dollar figure — it does not scale proportionally if the commitment amount is reduced. This has not yet been added to the committee packet, so the committee should be aware that even if we reduce the commitment to $5,000,000 to comply with the new cap Jonas just identified, the first capital call would still be $1,200,000.
